changes_made.explanation: Normalized method names, consolidated criteria to only those used for LLM-as-judge evaluation (entailment/faithfulness), removed relevance/grammaticality which were human eval criteria

guideline: For each sentence, raters evaluate: (1) entailment - whether the sentence can be deduced from the chart alone, (2) relevance - whether the sentence highlights important insights like min/max/avg values, (3) grammaticality - grammar, fluency, and repetition errors
Approximate numbers allowed up to 2 digits after decimal point

1. is_interesting highlights an important insight from the chart such as min / max / avg value or comparison. 2. cleaned_summary_is_grammatically_correct = grammar and fluency. 3. Entailed = you do not need additional info: using the chart only, be able to extract the text. 4. Approximate numbers is allowed up to 2 digits after the decimal. 5. grammatically_correct = look at grammar errors / fluency / repetition.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated guidelines into clear description, normalized criteria capitalization, added coherence which was implicitly evaluated at summary level

overall_notes: The paper focuses on chart-to-summary generation and evaluation. CHATS-CRITIC is the main contribution - a reference-free metric for evaluating chart summary faithfulness. The extraction was generally accurate but needed normalization and some consolidation. The paper clearly uses LLMs as judges (PaLM-2 for entailment verification) and conducts comprehensive human evaluations.
